title: Console/API: field-level validation errors for scaling policy (min>max, invalid cooldowns) + integration tests
author: Chloe Martin
description:
Problem
Console currently gets a generic 400 for several scaling-policy validation failures (e.g., min_replicas > max_replicas, cooldown out of range, malformed duration). That makes it hard to: (1) highlight the right fields in the UI, (2) provide actionable guidance to customers, and (3) reduce back-and-forth on support escalations.

This PR improves the validation error shape returned by the control-plane endpoints used by Console (Dedicated scaling policy) and adds integration tests covering the known bad inputs.

What changed
- Introduce structured, field-level validation errors for scaling policy writes:
  - Stable error codes (e.g., SCALING_POLICY_MIN_GT_MAX, SCALING_POLICY_COOLDOWN_OUT_OF_RANGE)
  - A JSON-pointer-like `field` path so Console can map the error to a specific input
  - Human-readable `message` suitable for surfacing in UI (no internal implementation details)
- Validation coverage for:
  - min_replicas > max_replicas
  - negative values
  - scale_up_cooldown_seconds and scale_down_cooldown_seconds outside allowed bounds
  - malformed numeric inputs (null/NaN strings in Console request payload)
- Add integration tests for the Console-facing API route that exercise the full request path (auth + RBAC + request validation + response mapping).

Example error response
POST /v1/dedicated/deployments/{deployment_id}/scaling-policy
HTTP 400
{
  "error": "validation_failed",
  "request_id": "req_01J4...",
  "details": [
    {
      "code": "SCALING_POLICY_MIN_GT_MAX",
      "field": "/bounds/min_replicas",
      "message": "min_replicas must be less than or equal to max_replicas"
    }
  ]
}

Notes / compatibility
- This preserves the top-level `error` string so existing clients don’t break.
- Console can opt into the new `details[]` mapping immediately; older Console builds will continue to show the generic error text.
- Error codes are treated as API surface area; please call out if naming should change.

Testing
- Added integration tests for invalid inputs and verified UI mapping manually in local Console (admin) build.
- Ran: unit, lint, and integration suites.

Rollout
- No feature flag required; only impacts invalid requests.
- Should reduce support load for ‘how to set bounds for SLA’ questions (SUP-28501) and speed up self-serve fixes.

Checklist
- [x] Added/updated tests
- [x] Verified RBAC behavior unchanged
- [x] Ensured error messages don’t leak internal policy evaluation details
- [x] Updated API docs inline (OpenAPI descriptions for error fields)
commits: control-plane: add ScalingPolicyValidationError codes + field paths
console-api: map validation errors into stable response shape
tests: integration coverage for bounds + cooldown validation
docs: update OpenAPI schema for validation_failed details
review_conversation:
Benji Okafor (requested changes): Can we guarantee code stability? Also please avoid returning multiple fields when the error is cross-field (min>max). Suggest pointing at min_replicas only and keeping max_replicas clean.
Chloe Martin (author): Agreed. Updated to emit a single detail for cross-field comparisons and documented codes as stable API surface in openapi.

Jordan Lee (requested changes): Cooldown bounds—what’s the canonical range? We should align with policy engine constants rather than duplicating in console-api.
Chloe Martin: Pulled bounds from capacity-policy-service constants and removed duplicate checks in console-api. Console-api now only does basic type coercion.

Tessa Morgan (comment): Message text should be short enough for inline form errors. ‘must be <=’ is fine; avoid mentioning internal units.
Chloe Martin: Adjusted messages + added examples in openapi descriptions.

Rafael Mendes (comment): Add at least one test that asserts request_id present for 400s; helps triage when customers paste screenshots.
Chloe Martin: Added assertions for request_id across validation_failed responses.

Felix Schneider (approval): UI mapping looks straightforward with field pointers; thanks for keeping error codes stable.

Approvals: Benji Okafor, Jordan Lee, Tessa Morgan, Rafael Mendes
